title: Signed Change Briefcase — PRD sketch
content:
Purpose

This doc proposes the 'Signed Change Briefcase' — a compact, signed artifact exchanged during customer-managed network or operator-initiated changes that:

- Captures a minimal, verifiable evidence bundle for a single logical change (config change, route update, firewall change).
- Serves both as the approval payload (used by the control plane to authorize an operation) and the audit record (immutable proof for later forensic queries).
- Minimizes telemetry footprint sent to Redwood while meeting customer audit needs and compliance constraints.

Why this exists (context)

We repeatedly hear customers asking for: lower telemetry retention, cryptographically verifiable audit packets they can store on their side, and a single artifact that can be used to:
 1) fast-approve or reject a planned change,
 2) provide an immutable evidence blob for postmortem and compliance, and
 3) allow lightweight forensic queries without replaying full packet traces.

Existing PRDs focus on large audit streams or operator evidence logs. This sketch focuses on a single-change compact exchange pattern to reduce storage, bandwidth, and PII exposure while preserving provability.

Goals

Primary:
- Design a concise, signed "briefcase" format (<= ~10KB typical) that proves: who proposed the change, which tenant and operator contexts apply, the before/after diff, and an approval decision (signed by an approver key).
- Provide APIs and operator UX to create, submit, inspect, and store briefcases.
- Ensure compatibility with customer-managed KMS/HSM for signing keys and with Redwood-managed keys for hosted flows.

Success metrics (initial)

- Average briefcase size <= 8KB for common network changes.
- 95th-percentile hub-to-control-plane validation latency < 200ms for briefcase-only approvals.
- 80% reduction in retained telemetry volume for customers who opt-in to briefcase-only retention mode.
- Zero escalations in first 3 pilot customers related to unverifiable audit evidence.

User stories

- As a private-deploy customer operator, I want to package a VPC route-table change into a signed briefcase so Redwood and my SOC can independently validate the change without sharing raw flow logs.
- As an on-call SRE at Redwood, I want to accept an incoming briefcase and validate it against our policy engine before applying the change to avoid blind rollouts.
- As a compliance auditor, I want to fetch the briefcase and verify the sequence of approver signatures and timestamps to produce an attestation report.

Non-goals

- This is not intended to replace full-fidelity packet-level forensic records or SIEM pipelines.
- Not intended to be the only audit mechanism for customers who require detailed flow telemetry retention by regulation.

High-level design

1) Briefcase structure (compact):
- header: version, briefcase_id (UUID), tenant_id, change_type, short description (string)
- context digest: hash pointer to optional larger payload stored by customer or Redwood (if allowed)
- change payload: minimal before/after diff (e.g., ACL rule add/remove)
- meta: actor_id (who proposed), actor_key_id, timestamp, policy-hash (reference to policy used to validate)
- approval block(s): list of signature entries (approver_id, approver_key_id, timestamp, signature)
- optional proof attributes: KMS key fingerprint, HSM attestation string (if provided)

Implementation notes: briefcase is JSON Lz4-compressed and canonicalized before signing to keep size small and signatures deterministic. Use a canonical serialization (RFC8785-like) for deterministic canonical JSON.

2) Signing model:
- Primary flows:
  a) Customer-managed signing: customer operator signs the proposal with their key (stored in customer KMS). The operator then requests Redwood approver (could be automated policy engine) to sign acceptance. The final briefcase contains both signatures.
  b) Redwood-managed signing (hosted/dedicated): Redwood signs approval with staff signing key; customer may still provide initial proposer signature.
- Key types supported: ECDSA P-256, Ed25519. Support KMS/HSM key identifiers and signature envelopes.

3) Approval gates and validation:
- On briefcase submission, Redwood runs synchronous policy checks (policy-hash included in briefcase) and verifies chain of signatures.
- If short-circuit policies exist (trusted-operator, pre-approved templates), acceptance can be automatic. Otherwise briefcase remains in pending state until a human approver signs.
- Rejection: an approver signs a rejection briefcase referencing original briefcase_id and a rejection code.

4) Storage/retention and privacy:
- Default: store the briefcase (signed artifact) for 365 days (configurable).
- Option: customer-only retention mode — briefcases are exchanged but Redwood stores only a hash and index; customer stores the blob. Redwood will keep minimal index + verifiable checkpoint to satisfy support while keeping telemetry minimal.
- Redaction: fields that contain customer PII (freeform descriptions) can be redacted and replaced with a digest; original stored in customer vault if needed.

APIs (proposal)

- POST /v1/private/briefcases (submit briefcase blob) -> { briefcase_id, status }
- GET /v1/private/briefcases/{id} -> { briefcase blob | index-only metadata }
- POST /v1/private/briefcases/{id}/sign -> { approver_signature } (for authorized approvers)
- GET /v1/private/briefcases?tenant={id}&since={ts} -> list of briefcase_ids + metadata

Example briefcase (human-readable excerpt):

{
  "briefcase_id": "b2d7f9c4-...",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-acme",
  "change_type": "route-table-update",
  "change_payload": "{diff: [+10.0.0.0/24 -> via gw-3]}",
  "actor_id": "operator/weekly-ops",
  "approvals": [
    {"approver_id": "policy-engine/v1", "signature": "BASE64(sig)", "ts": "2024-12-01T13:22:08Z"},
    {"approver_id": "oncall/jake", "signature": "BASE64(sig)", "ts": "2024-12-01T13:25:53Z"}
  ]
}

Operational UX

- Console: a "Briefcases" tab under Private > Onboarding & Changes listing that shows pending briefcases, who signed, expected impact, and quick-accept (auto-apply) when policy passes.
- CLI tool: rwi-ctl briefcase pack | submit | sign | fetch — convenience helpers for customers operating on-prem.
- Rollback: support dual-briefcase pattern where the rollback briefcase references original briefcase_id and contains inverse diff.

Security & compliance considerations

- Timestamping: include NTP-synced timestamps and an optional anchor into a tamper-evident timeline (blockchain-like checkpoint or Redwood immutable ledger) for high-assurance customers.
- Key compromise: rotate signing keys, maintain signature revocation lists; briefcase validation must check key status via KMS/HSM introspection.
- Least privilege: approver roles enforced via RBAC and signed authorization tokens.

Threat model high-level

- Tampering in transit: use TLS + briefcase signature verification.
- Replay attacks: briefcase_id + nonce + short TTL on pending briefcase states.
- Rogue approver: require multi-approver for high-risk changes.

Compatibility and integration

- Integrate with existing private-deploy attestation CLI and onboarding flows.
- Provide conversion tools to generate briefcases from existing audit events for a transition path.

Testing and pilot plan

- Unit tests: briefcase generation, canonicalization, signature verification for supported key types.
- End-to-end: pilot with 2 customers (one on VPC-only, one with on-prem operatorless setup) for 3 months. Measure briefcase size, latency, rollback correctness.
- Compliance review: get SOC/Privacy signoff and list of fields considered PII.

Rollout milestones (quarterly)

- Q1: v0 sketch + API proto + internal dogfood (SRE + 1 pilot)
- Q2: KMS/HSM bindings + console UX + 2 external pilots
- Q3: retention modes and immutable checkpointing opt-in + broader release

Open questions / TODOs

- Should briefcase canonicalization require a stricter schema (protobuf) to avoid JSON edge-cases? (TODO: prototyping).
- Policy-hash validation: how do we safely refer to policy versions across air-gapped customers? (Action: @Lucia to propose policy fingerprinting scheme).
- Decision: default retention 365 days vs customer-configurable 90/365/0 (index-only) — propose defaults and guardrails.
- UX: smart diff summarization for console display (TOOLING: generate human-friendly summary from diff).

Linked tickets / refs

- Linear: PD-574 (briefcase proto)
- GitHub PR: rwi#432 (briefcase canonicalization helper)
- Slack thread: #priv-deploy-ops pinned messages (see thread ts 1701203800.000100)

Notes to self

- Keep briefcase small = adoption wins. If we require lots of extra attributes, this loses the bandwidth & privacy advantages.
- Pilot offer: let early customers opt for "index-only" Redwood storage + local briefcase retention in exchange for product credit.

-- end of sketch --

Unresolved: see Open questions above. Will iterate after architecture sync with infra and SRE (scheduled 2024-12-15).
